provenance.source: 150 g times standard gravity 9.80665 m/s2 (a defined constant) is 1.471 N (computed), rounded to 1.47; 150 g is the owner's design target "Accessibility switch, 150 g press" (fab-knowledge/plan-v5/old-skills-scenarios.md line 17), a target and not a measured feel; read by the access switch force claim (R1-flagship-access-switch-04)

design band either side of access.pressTargetN, 1.18 to 1.76 N or 120 to 180 g (computed); chosen to match click.modulusSpreadPct so the drawn point can sit inside it while the modulus is a working value; no coupon recorded; read by the access switch force claim (R1-flagship-access-switch-04)

diametral clearance of the access switch paddle in its guide: the PIP click row "cap through bezel hole" 0.5 diametral (packages/archetypes/src/pip/click.ts line 91) less one 0.1 mm step because the paddle guide is longer than the bezel hole; no coupon recorded; read by the access switch design (R1-flagship-access-switch-02)

highest pin voltage, as a fraction of the input supply, that a switch interface reads as pressed: the lower edge of the BLOCKS undefined band, 0.3 VIO (fab-knowledge:originals/blocks/files/src-extracted/app2.js line 383, lineage blocks.app2/blocks-1), the common CMOS VIL; no switch interface datasheet on record (inferred); read by the access switch contact closure read (R1-score-05)

the pull a switch interface input holds its 3.5 mm tip to: the BLOCKS sim PULLUP element, 50e3 from the pin to VIO (fab-knowledge:originals/blocks/files/src-extracted/sim.js line 94, lineage blocks.sim/blocks-1), and the Teensy or ESP internal 45 kohm of knowledge/00-constants.md; no Xbox Adaptive Controller, AbleNet or iPad switch adapter datasheet on record gives its pullup, so an MCU internal pull stands in (inferred); read by the access switch contact closure read (R1-score-05)

highest closed resistance an adapted toy (a battery interrupter in series with its motor) runs through: two AA cells, 3 V, a small toy DC motor at 0.2 A running, and no more than 10 percent of the supply lost in the switch, 0.3 V over 0.2 A is 1.5 ohm (computed from inferred inputs); no toy or interrupter datasheet on record; read by the access switch contact closure read (R1-score-05)
